-A.help: is available on systems configured for AFS whose AFS kernel code is implemented via dynamic modules. It allows the user to specify as an alternate name list file where the kernel addresses of the dynamic modules might be found. See the FAQ (The FAQ section gives its location.) for more information about dynamic modules, their symbols, and how they affect

-C.help: disables the reporting of any path name components from the kernel's name cache. See the section for more information.

-D.help: directs use of the device cache file. The use of this option is sometimes restricted. See the section and the sections that follow it for more information on this option.

-F.help: specifies a character list, that selects the fields to be output for processing by another program, and the character that terminates each output field. Each field to be output is specified with a single character in The field terminator defaults to NL, but may be changed to NUL (000). See the section for a description of the field identification characters and the field output process.

-H.help: directs lsof to print human readable sizes, e.g. 123.4K 456.7M.

-J.help: selects JSON output mode.  Instead of the traditional tabular or field output, lsof produces a single JSON object on stdout containing a array.  Each process object contains its fields and a array of open file entries.

-K.help: selects the listing of tasks (threads) of processes, on dialects where task (thread) reporting is supported. (If help output - i.e., the output of the or options - shows this option, then task (thread) reporting is supported by the dialect.)

-N.help: selects the listing of NFS files.

-O.help: directs to bypass the strategy it uses to avoid being blocked by some kernel operations - i.e., doing them in forked child processes. See the and sections for more information on kernel operations that may block

-P.help: inhibits the conversion of port numbers to port names for network files (the mapping is commonly learned from /etc/services). Inhibiting the conversion may make run a little faster. It is also useful when port name lookup is not working properly.

-Q.help: ignore failed search terms. When is told to search for users of a file, or for users of a device, or for a specific PID, or for certain protocols in use by that PID, and so on, will return an error if any of the search results are empty. The option will change this behavior so that will instead return a successful exit code (0) even if any of the search results are empty. In addition, missing search terms will not be reported to stderr.

-R.help: directs lsof to list the Parent Process IDentification number in the PPID column.

-S.help: specifies an optional time-out seconds value for kernel functions - and - that might otherwise deadlock. The minimum for is two; the default, fifteen; when no value is specified, the default is used.

-T.help: controls the reporting of some TCP/TPI information, also reported by following the network addresses. In normal output the information appears in parentheses, each item except TCP or TPI state name identified by a keyword, followed by `=', separated from others by a single space:

-U.help: selects the listing of UNIX domain socket files.

-V.help: directs to indicate the items it was asked to list and failed to find - command names, file names, Internet addresses or files, login names, NFS files, PIDs, PGIDs, and UIDs.

-X.help: This is a dialect-specific option. AIX: This IBM AIX RISC/System 6000 option requests the reporting of executed text file and shared library references.

-Z.help: specifies how SELinux security contexts are to be handled. It and 'Z' field output character support are inhibited when SELinux is disabled in the running Linux kernel. See for more information on the 'Z' field output character.

-a.help: causes list selection options to be ANDed, as described above.

-c.help: selects the listing of files for processes executing the command that begins with the characters of Multiple commands may be specified, using multiple options. They are joined in a single ORed set before participating in AND option selection.

-d.help: specifies a list of file descriptors (FDs) to exclude from or include in the output listing. The file descriptors are specified in the comma-separated set &- e.g., ``cwd,1,3'', ``^6,^2''. (There should be no spaces in the set.)

-g.help: excludes or selects the listing of files for the processes whose optional process group IDentification (PGID) numbers are in the comma-separated set &- e.g., ``123'' or ``123,^456''. (There should be no spaces in the set.)

-i.help: selects the listing of files any of whose Internet address matches the address specified in i. If no address is specified, this option selects the listing of all Internet and x.25 (HP-UX) network files.

-j.help: selects JSON Lines output mode.  Each open file produces one JSON object per line, combining process and file fields in a single denormalized record.  This format is suitable for streaming pipelines, log ingestion (Splunk, Datadog, Elastic), and line-oriented tools.

-k.help: specifies a kernel name list file, in place of /vmunix, /mach, etc. is not available under AIX on the IBM RISC/System 6000.

-l.help: inhibits the conversion of user ID numbers to login names. It is also useful when login name lookup is working improperly or slowly.

-n.help: inhibits the conversion of network numbers to host names for network files. Inhibiting conversion may make run faster. It is also useful when host name lookup is not working properly.

-o.help: defines the number of decimal digits (o) to be printed after the ``0t'' for a file offset before the form is switched to ``0x...''. An value of zero (unlimited) directs to use the ``0t'' form for all offset output.

-p.help: excludes or selects the listing of files for the processes whose optional process IDentification (PID) numbers are in the comma-separated set &- e.g., ``123'' or ``123,^456''. (There should be no spaces in the set.)

-s.help: alone directs to display file size at all times. It causes the SIZE/OFF output column title to be changed to SIZE. If the file does not have a size, nothing is displayed.

-t.help: produce terse output comprising only process identifiers (without a header), so that it is easy to use programmatically. e.g. # reload anything using old SSL lsof -t /lib/*/libssl.so.* | xargs -r kill -HUP # get list of processes and then iterate over them (Bash only) mapfile -t pids < <( lsof -wt /var/log/your.log ) for pid in "${pids[@]}" ; do your_command -p "$pid" done The option implies the option.

-u.help: selects the listing of files for the user whose login names or user ID numbers are in the comma-separated set &- e.g., ``abe'', or ``548,root''. (There should be no spaces in the set.)

-v.help: selects the listing of version information, including: revision number; when the binary was constructed; who constructed the binary and where; the name of the compiler used to construct the the version number of the compiler when readily available; the compiler and loader flags used to construct the binary; and system information, typically the output of option.
